messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Ceres Finance (enterprise, VPC eu2, dedicated pool) p99 latency breach detected — p95 320ms -> 1.8s, p99 4.9s. Error ratio still low. Paging oncall.

alex-nguyen: I’m on it. seeing sustained queue depth on pool ceres-eu2-dedicated-01, GPU utilization ~98% on two hosts.

samira: tagging infra: looks like one host spiking mem usage, OOM kills for worker 12 at 08:12:43 UTC. logs attached -> `worker_12: evicting KV cache` then `OOM`.

lee-kim: adding context — customer traffic doubled (their spike) + long context windows (many 8k token requests). Batching params tuned for 2k tokens; hitting bad tail.

taylor-p: customer impact: Ceres reports queueing in their app, intermittent 5xx from our gateway. CS on call.

maya-chen: @taylor-p I pinged the Ceres SE, they confirm degraded checkout latency for ~15% of sessions. They want ETA.

alex-nguyen: immediate mitigations we can try: 1) Evict noisy tenant from shared nodes -> move to isolated spare. 2) Autoscale dedicated pool (if capacity available in region). 3) Route new requests to fallback model variant with lower memory footprint/quantized. Starting 1 and 3 now.

naresh: running tenant isolation playbook. command:
```
rbctl tenant isolate --tenant ceres-finance --pool ceres-eu2-dedicated-01 --target spare-isol-01
```

naresh: isolation started. draining connections from worker_12 -> will reject new connections to that worker and spin up isol-01.

incident-bot: Action logged: tenant isolation initiated by naresh at 08:18:02 UTC.

lee-kim: concurrently triggering fallback routing. patching routing policy to prefer `redwood-opt-quant-v2` for tenant ceres-finance for new sessions.

samira: watch on OOMs. If memory compacts after isolation, we may not need a full pool scale.

taylor-p: FYI Ceres SE says they can tolerate a model downgrade for 30m if it buys stability. Approve switching.

alex-nguyen: switching live now. `routes.update(tenant='ceres-finance', model='redwood-opt-quant-v2', mode='prefer')` -> applied.

incident-bot: Routing change deployed (id: chg-9853). Telemetry will reflect new model within ~30s.

maya-chen: relaying to Ceres: told them we’re isolating noisy host and routing to a smaller model. asked for any spike drivers on their side.

lee-kim: telemetry tick: p95 down to 420ms, p99 down to 1.1s after routing change and partial isolation. still seeing a subset of long tails from in-flight sessions.

samira: OOM frequency dropped after worker_12 drained. host mem stable now. cluster reports free GPU slots on isol-01.

naresh: started scale-up if needed: `rbctl pool scale ceres-eu2-dedicated-01 --add 2 --reason "emergency spike"` — pending approval from autoscale policy, but we have spare quota.

alex-nguyen: approving manual scale. please finalize.

naresh: scale applied. two new nodes provisioning; expected ready ~6m.

taylor-p: CS confirms Ceres saw improvement in their next samples. they still see occasional 2s responses for very long contexts; likely sessions that started pre-change.

lee-kim: recommendation: keep fallback routing for 20m, let new nodes warm, then migrate long-running sessions off older nodes. also we should run a short eval later to validate quality delta.

maya-chen: Ceres asked for RCA and timeline. I'll start a customer note: will include mitigation steps, timeframe, and whether rate-limits or prompt shims recommended.

incident-bot: Timeline note: 08:12 alert -> 08:18 isolation -> 08:20 routing change -> 08:26 p95 improved -> 08:32 scale nodes online (est)

samira: quick log snippet from drained worker:
```
[08:16:51] worker_12: long request id=zz-4432 len=7800 tokens
[08:16:58] worker_12: KV cache flush
[08:17:03] worker_12: OOM -> restart
```

lee-kim: postmortem likely root cause = combination of sudden tenant traffic + unusually long contexts causing memory pressure + batching misaligned for 8k sessions. mitigations: tenant isolation, fallback model, scale pool.

alex-nguyen: action items:
- alex: formalise temporary routing rollback plan (done at 20m).
- samira: collect OOM traces and kernel logs, attach to incident.
- lee: recommend batching config for long-context sessions and add auto-quant fallback when mem>90%.
- maya: customer comms + RCA draft.
- naresh: verify nodes healthy and decommission any unstable worker.

oncall-maria: taking handoff. I’ll monitor the next hour and own postmortem. @alex-nguyen please assign any follow-ups to SRE board.

alex-nguyen: handing off to oncall-maria. All consoles and runbooks linked here: https://redwood.internal/incidents/4311122355

taylor-p: marking customer impact: moderate (checkout latency degraded, partial sessions affected). CS follow-up scheduled. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity lowered from P1 to P2 at 08:34 UTC.

oncall-maria: notes for morning: validate autoscale thresholds, add guard to prevent >2x sudden tenant spike without prewarmed nodes for long-context models.

maya-chen: Ceres accepted plan, want weekly sync next Tue. will coordinate.

alex-nguyen: thanks team. closing war-room buffer; keep thread for postmortem artifacts.

oncall-maria: closing handoff. I’ll update `postmortems/4311122355` with details within 48h.
